title: Negative possession questions review
focus: Mix the forms and sentence patterns already taught in this pack.
targetSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions

exercises.prompt: Choose “Don’t you have a ball?” in Finnish. Use sinulla (“you as the owner”) and palloa (“a ball”). Frame: “___ sinulla ole palloa”. Address one person.
exercises.explanation: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form.
requiredSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.targetSkill: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.Eikö sinulla ole palloa?: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form.
optionFeedback.Eivätkö sinulla ole palloa?: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form. This choice uses the wrong verb form.
optionFeedback.Eikö sinulla on palloa?: This choice changes the required polarity or leaves the required question pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: sinä has the learned possession form sinulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.

exercises.prompt: Build “Don’t you have a ball?” Put the owner immediately after the question word. Use sinulla (“you as the owner”) and palloa (“a ball”). Address one person.
exercises.explanation: Follow the pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun.

exercises.prompt: Reply to “Eikö sinulla ole palloa?” with “You do have it.” Use a verb reply; Kyllä or Ei is optional. pallo means “ball”. Address one person.
exercises.explanation: Answer the stated possession meaning: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies having it. Both remain fixed with every owner. An optional Kyllä or Ei can introduce the reply.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: fixed possession verb reply; owner and thing understood from the question

parts.formation: Kyllä means “yes”; it can introduce the affirmative verb reply.
Echo fixed on: the owner and thing are understood from the question.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Olen and en ole describe “I am” and “I am not”. A possession reply echoes fixed on or ei ole.
